{{MEinfobox|name=Fragile & Resist Down|cg=Fragile.png}}'''Fragile''', its variants, and the types of '''Resist Down''' are negative statuses which directly increase the damage dealt to the afflicted target.

{{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}} causes Skill damage to be increased by 10% per Count (to a maximum of 100% extra damage), and expires at the end of the turn.
There are three types of Fragility for a total of eleven effects: 
* The standard {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}}, which increases all damage taken.
* Three {{StatusEffect|Slash Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Blunt Fragility|x}} Damage Type Fragilities that increase [[Slash]], [[Pierce]] and [[Blunt]] damage respectively.
* Seven {{StatusEffect|Wrath Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Lust Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Sloth Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Gluttony Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Gloom Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Pride Fragility|x}}{{StatusEffect|Envy Fragility|x}} Sin Affinity Fragilities that increase damage from each [[Sin]] Affinity.

Resist Down (e.g. {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}}) status effects increase enemy Resistances and function similarly to Fragilities, but apply to a different part of the damage calculation formula. In comparison to {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}}, Resist Down is more effective against enemies resistant to the Damage Type but less effective against enemies that are already weak to the Damage Type.

==Strengths & Weaknesses==
{{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}} is a powerful status effect that can significantly increase damage dealt to an enemy. Its main limitation is that it expires at Turn End and has a Max Stack of 10, preventing any given Fragility effect from increasing damage by more than 100%. Due to its strength, {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}} is often limited to powerful Skills, or replaced by more restricted effects such as {{StatusEffect|Blunt Fragility|d}}.

Different types of Fragility can be stacked for additive bonuses. For example, an enemy with 8 {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}} and 8 {{StatusEffect|Slash Fragility|d}} would take +160% damage from Slash Skills that turn, surpassing the theoretical cap of +100% damage. 

In [[Mirror Dungeon]], large amounts of Fragility can be applied by combining multiple E.G.O Gifts, greatly increasing the amount of damage your team deals. Outside of Mirror Dungeon, it is difficult to get large or consistent values for Fragility effects.

==Damage Calculations: Fragile vs. Resist Down==
Fragility and Resist Down effects apply to the damage calculation formula differently. Specifically, Fragility changes the dynamic modifier while Resist Down changes the static modifier. Effects like {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}} directly changes the resistance modifier, while effects like {{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|d}} add an additional damage multiplier after resistances are taken into account. This creates the following results:
* If an enemy is resistant to a damage type (ex. <span style="color:#808080;">Ineff. [x0.5]</span> ), Resist Down is more effective. 
* If an enemy is weak to a damage type (ex. <span style="color:red;">Fatal [x2]</span> ), Fragility is nearly twice as effective as Resist Down.
* If an enemy is netural to the damage type (ex. <span style="color:#edcda4;">Normal [x1]</span> ), there is no difference between the two. 

This is difficult to compare without an example. Let's say a Pierce Attack Skill will deal exactly 100 base damage. For simplicity, we'll also say that the Skill has no Sin Affinity and that the Offense Level of the attacker is equal to the Defense Level of the target. This gives us the following simplified damage formula:

{|
|-
| '''Final Damage = Base Damage x Static Modifier x Dynamic Modifier'''
|}

Now we can look at a specific example for the three distinct scenarios.

{| style="text-align:center; border:1px solid #810000; border-radius:7.5px"
|+ '''An Enemy with <span style="color:#808080;">Ineff. [x0.5]</span> Pierce Resistance'''<ref>An enemy with resistance between 0 and 1 has its modifier changed by <math> \tfrac{x - 1}{2} </math>, so an enemy  <span style="color:#808080;">Ineff. [x0.5]</span>  to a damage type takes 25% less damage, not 50% less damage.  </ref>
|-
|  || Base Damage || x || Static Modifier || x || Dynamic Modifier || = || Result
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}} || 100 || x || 0.95 || x || 1 || = || 95 damage
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|d}} || 100 || x || 0.75 || x || 1.2 || = || 90 damage
|}

{| style="text-align:center; border:1px solid #810000; border-radius:7.5px"
|+ '''An Enemy with <span style="color:#edcda4;">Normal [x1]</span> Pierce Resistance'''
|-
|  || Base Damage || x || Static Modifier || x || Dynamic Modifier || = || Result
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}} || 100 || x || 1.2 || x || 1 || = || 120 damage
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|d}} || 100 || x || 1 || x || 1.2 || = || 120 damage
|}

{| style="text-align:center; border:1px solid #810000; border-radius:7.5px"
|+ '''An Enemy with <span style="color:red;">Fatal [x2]</span> Pierce Resistance'''
|-
|  || Base Damage || x || Static Modifier || x || Dynamic Modifier || = || Result
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}} || 100 || x || 2.2 || x || 1 || = || 220 damage
|-
| 2 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|d}} || 100 || x || 2 || x || 1.2 || = || 240 damage
|}


It is worth noting that different types of Fragility (and all other damage modifiers, such as {{StatusEffect|Damage Up|b}} and Skill conditionals) can stack, and will continue to change the dynamic modifier. For example, having 10 stacks of {{StatusEffect|Pierce Fragility|d}}, {{StatusEffect|Fragile|d}}, and {{StatusEffect|Delicateness|d}} simultaneously would result in an incoming Pierce attack having a dynamic modifier of 4.0 (i.e. +300% damage). Resist Down effects can stack in a similar way, but require specific combinations of Attack Type and Sin Affinity. For example, the static modifier could be theoretically modified by +2.0 by combining 10 {{StatusEffect|Pierce Resist Down|d}} and {{StatusEffect|Gloom Resist Down|d}}, but this would only provide its full benefit when using exactly a Pierce Gloom Skill.
